slides.0.title: Climate, Soils and Viticulture
slides.0.subtitle: Semi-continental vs Mediterranean
slides.1.title: Northern Rhône: semi-continental and steep
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Semi-continental climate
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Cooler winters and warm summers with Mediterranean influence that varies; Côte-Rôtie's climate is close to Lyon's, leaning continental
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Ancient rock
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Mostly granite, gneiss and schist; Côte-Rôtie is largely metamorphic rock, Hermitage granitic sand with clay and loess
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Steep terraces
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Steep slopes are held by dry-stone terrace walls (chaillées); machines struggle to enter, so labour demand is high
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Échalas stake training
slides.1.highlights.3.content: Traditionally each Syrah vine is tied to its own stake (échalas) to withstand wind and suit steep slopes
slides.1.content: Steep slopes, ancient rock and hand work explain why the north is costly, small and expensive.
slides.2.title: Southern Rhône: Mediterranean climate, varied soils
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Hot, dry summers
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Plenty of sun and low rainfall; Châteauneuf-du-Pape gets under about 650 mm of rain and around 2,800 sun hours (single source, WineWithSeth; approximate)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Galets roulés
slides.2.highlights.1.content: The famous rounded stones of Châteauneuf-du-Pape absorb heat by day and release it at night, aiding ripening
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Varied sedimentary soils
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Sand, marl, limestone, clay and gravel sit side by side, so village styles differ widely
slides.2.highlights.3.title: Gobelet bush vines
slides.2.highlights.3.content: Low bush-trained gobelet vines are common in the south, reducing wind impact and shading fruit, especially for old-vine Grenache
slides.2.content: The south is about heat and wind: high ripeness and alcohol, with a rounded style.
slides.3.title: The Mistral: a shared key factor
slides.3.highlights.0.title: A cold, dry northerly
slides.3.highlights.0.content: The Mistral blows down the valley from north to south, affecting both halves and most strongly the south
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Benefits
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Dries the vines, reduces disease pressure and clears the skies, increasing sunshine
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Risks
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Strong wind can snap shoots and hurt fruit set, hence stake training and low vine shapes
slides.3.content: A common exam point: the Mistral is a terroir factor that brings healthy fruit and shapes viticulture.
slides.4.title: Organic and sustainability (2025)
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Organic and biodynamic
slides.4.highlights.0.content: 2025 harvest: about 24% of volume and 26% of area (Inter Rhône body text; the cover says 25%, so treat as approximate)
slides.4.highlights.1.title: HVE certification
slides.4.highlights.1.content: HVE (High Environmental Value) level 3 covers about 37% of volume and 34% of area
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Why organic is easier here
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Dry, windy conditions lower disease pressure, making organic farming comparatively easy
slides.4.content: Figures are annual and change; quizzes ask concepts such as why organic is easier here.
slides.5.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
What is the main positive effect of the Mistral on Rhône vineyards?
B. Drying the vines and lowering disease pressure
The dry, strong Mistral lowers mildew risk; the downside is possible shoot damage.
Where are the famous rounded stones (galets roulés) of Châteauneuf-du-Pape found?
The stones belong to the southern Rhône, storing heat by day and releasing it at night.
Which description of northern vs southern Rhône is correct?
A. North: pebbly plains; south: granite slopes
C. North: semi-continental with steep terraces; south: Mediterranean with more open terrain
The north is semi-continental with steep ancient-rock slopes; the south is Mediterranean, flatter, with varied soils.
